a:r.a:t: Structurally, these two enzymes are different than those in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis (i.e., they are conjoined, rather than independent) and are regulated via phosphorylation.

p:cNvPr.descr: In (b), at the top is a blue angled rectangle identified as PFK-2 (active). It has 14 lines shooting out all around it, with the last one identified as OH. A regular blue reactangle is directly below that identified as FBPase-2 (inactive). The blue rectangles have a slightly curved arrow on the right, with cAMP-dependent protein kinase (in blue) in the middle, that points to another set of blue rectangles. The top regular rectangle is identified as PFK-2 (inactive) and the bottom angles rectangle is identified as FBPase-2 (active). This rectangle has 14 lines shooting off all around it with the top one on the right showing O bonding right to P, which binds right to O- and down to O-. P also double binds up to O. To the right of the arrow going down from the first set of rectangles is another more extremely curved arrow (opposite curve direction) that begins with ATP pointing to ADP. In the middle of the arrow is a green rectangle in a circle that has a dashed arrow pointing to it entitled glucagon ([up arrow] [cAMP]). To the left of the arrow pointing up from the blue rectangles at the bottom is another more severely curved arrow that begins with H2O at the bottom pointing up to P1. In the middle of that arrow is a green rectangle in a circle that has a dashed arrow pointing to it entitled insulin. Above that arrow is a purple box with an [up arrow][F26BP] at the top, and "Stimulates glycolysis, inhibits gluconeogenesis" written inside. Below that arrow and to the left the bottom blue rectangles is another purple box with [down arrow][F26BP] at the top and "Inhibits glycolysis, stimulates gluconeogenesis" written inside.
